design_rationale:
TASK 0 DOSSIER (prime_enrollment_fees_and_pcm, M=2). Worklog kept from Step 0; reworked in round 2 after the policy-task audit.

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0055_military_health_plan_administrator/prime_enrollment_fees_and_pcm/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 5, 5]}. Every problem of this tree carries 5 factors.

[Why this is a good test] Gordon asks for one thing - the fees for the months his reinstated Prime coverage was restored put on his card on file. The agent must discover from the draft policy's prerequisite sentences that (1) no installment covers the restored months yet (a catch-up must first be posted, its span and value decided by the Enrollment Reinstatement Review in the appeal records and by his short TRICARE Select stint), (2) a duplicate April payment stands and must be refunded before any draft, and (3) the October installment is short and must be paid in full - by the beneficiary himself through a one-time bank draft - before the back-billed installment may be drawn. Each write is a 5-factor computation over a reinstated account (a late review decision, medical records in the case file, a July Select stint, a 75.00 bill-pay duplicate partly refunded, a February transfer partly refunded, an October payment left short, a card that has not collected since the reinstatement). Difficulty comes from reading rules and reconciling the ledger, never from picking among similar tools: each hidden tool is named by exactly one policy.

[Scope - occupied / claimed / reserved] It claims prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up (post_catch_up_installment_4baf2609), prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund (refund_duplicate_payment_360f0d4a), prime_ext_current_installment_payment (pay_current_installment_by_bank_draft_694809d0, owner=user) and prime_ext_draft_on_file_method (run_draft_on_file_method_99529347). Task 1 claims the four other extended policies; no policy or tool is shared. The charter splits enrollments by the plan year they took effect in, so every prerequisite state has exactly one policy that can bring it about: the catch-up, the draft and the one-time payment act only on an enrollment that took effect before the current plan year; the first-installment supplement, the first-installment duplicate refund and the initial payment act only on one that took effect in the current plan year; the duplicate refund leaves the first installment of a current-plan-year enrollment to the first-installment duplicate refund. Gordon's enrollment took effect 2020-01-01, so all four of this task's policies act on it and none of task 1's does.

[Problem-tree card] Root: prime_ext_draft_on_file_method (on_request; the customer's surface request). Prerequisite problems: prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up (state_due), prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund (state_due), prime_ext_current_installment_payment (state_due, owner=user tool). Fan-out; topological order prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up -> prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund -> prime_ext_current_installment_payment -> prime_ext_draft_on_file_method (the three prerequisites commute).
 Edge 1 prime_ext_draft_on_file_method<-prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up: value_input, gate dd_target, form state. Sentence: "A draft toward a back-billed installment is made only after an installment charge on the account has a coverage period that reaches the month before the current month." Connective "only after"; record-visible state (a charge's coverage period reaching the month before the current month); names no action, performer or tool; false at frozen time (no coverage includes September 2026).
 Edge 2 prime_ext_draft_on_file_method<-prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund: value_input, gate dd_off, form action. Sentence: "No draft is made on an account until the region has made the duplicate refund owed on it, wherever that refund comes to more than nothing." fallback_reason: a 2.00 refund already stands against the duplicate, so a record-visible "refund against the duplicate" would already hold; only the region's refund of the duplicate itself can carry the dependency, and the sentence states that no act is awaited where the refund owed comes to nothing (one reading on every account).
 Edge 3 prime_ext_draft_on_file_method<-prime_ext_current_installment_payment: state_gate, gate prime_fee_ledger.amount, form state. Sentence: "The region does not draw a back-billed installment until the installment of the current month stands paid in full." Connective "until"; record-visible state (payments less refunds on the current month's installment reaching its charge); false at frozen time (20.00 of 32.51).
 Value-input edges 2 of 3 (floor max(3-1, 1) = 2). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip catch-up -> draft 0.00; skip duplicate refund -> draft 47.04; skip October payment -> draft 65.02 with the state gate unmet. The tool layer validates none of these.

[Factor card] (tier taken -> figure; baseline figure in brackets). The monthly rate is not a factor: it is one twelfth of the annual fee of the enrollment's recorded fee arrangement (individual, 390.12 -> 32.51), as the base fee schedule sets it.
 Catch-up (expected 113.54, all-baseline 227.57): first month April (May the first month billed) - medical records, no proof of payment [81.03]; region bears August - decided 55 days after filing, deadline 30 [146.05]; Select only touches July - billed less Select's share [130.04]; Select's share 16.50, a monthly Select installment [128.66]; monthly arrangement bills per month [227.57].
 Duplicate refund (expected 17.98, all-baseline 0.0): installment April - largest non-card payment [0.0]; value one twelfth [0.0]; returns the latest 75.00 bill-pay transfer [8.0]; the 2.00 refund against it comes off (plumbing); one regular installment kept, recurring card with card collections [50.49], valued at one twelfth [0.0].
 One-time payment (expected 45.02, all-baseline 390.12): October, the latest monthly installment [422.63]; one twelfth [402.63]; ahead installment valued at one twelfth, the card's last collection being monthly [402.63]; lapse judged from April, the month after the review's old paid-through date [12.51]; one regular installment ahead, the card having collected nothing since [12.51].
 Draft (expected 65.02, all-baseline 0.0): toward the catch-up [0.0]; regular installment 32.51 [113.54]; at most two regular installments, recurring card with card collections [113.54]; history from April [59.02] (payments and refunds over the look-back after 2026-03-14, charges beginning April through September, the last closed month); its excess of 32.51 is the one regular installment the region keeps for the next installment because the card has collected [32.51], so nothing comes off.
 Per-task floors: multi-source factors duplicate_amount_kept, one_time_payment_months_ahead and draft_limit_by_method (each tier joins the method on file with the ledger's collections); cross-difficulty factors catch_up_first_month and catch_up_months_region_bears (appeal), catch_up_select_coverage and catch_up_select_share (select), one_time_payment_lapse_window and draft_history_window (appeal). Every tier is decided from ledger aggregates, dates, the appeal case file or the Select records; the only enrollment fields read are the arrangement's frequency and method, which name no outcome.

[Base-invariant card] Catch-up (prime_fee_charge): prime_enrollment_fee_schedule.fee_bearing_enrollment_open - "Installments are charged only on a fee-bearing enrollment whose status is applied or active." - evidence initial_state.prime_enrollments.d51c2b68-4bca-482d-8c49-21471cda6fa7.status = active, fee_bearing = true; overwrite declared for the clause on installment periods. Duplicate refund (prime_fee_refund): prime_fee_proration_credit scope only; overwrite declared for the refund-of-credit-balance clause (the region keeps regular installments on the account). One-time payment and draft (prime_fee_payment): prime_fee_payment_methods.method_allowed_for_frequency - "The payment method on a fee payment is one the tier accepts for the enrollment's installment frequency." - electronic funds transfer and recurring card are monthly methods of Group A - and prime_nonpayment_disenrollment scope; overwrites declared for 'oldest unpaid installment first and never to a future period' (the current-installment rule, the month paid ahead and the draft's back-billed target).

[Business-object card] Holding: Gordon's only Prime enrollment d51c2b68-4bca-482d-8c49-21471cda6fa7. Catch-up: May-September 2026, August borne by the region, July less Select's share, April already charged. Duplicate: the April installment c2d80912-5ece-4de3-8b8f-03373e5f8e0a, its 75.00 payment 3d6ebbce-35a2-474f-ac59-3db7b7810642. One-time payment: the October installment fb771c45-ea4f-4088-9061-611aebe70710. Draft: the catch-up row created at step 10.

[Seed design] Customer row (single enrollee: one customer lookup is allowed), one Prime enrollment (active, monthly recurring card, individual), 16 ledger rows (December-March charges with card payments, a February 10.00 transfer refunded 4.00 in March, the April charge with a 10.00 transfer and a 75.00 bill-pay transfer refunded 2.00, the October charge with a 20.00 transfer), the reinstatement review (filed 2026-06-10, decided overturned 2026-08-04, old paid-through 2026-03-31) with a statement of good cause and medical records, the July Select enrollment (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-12) with its 16.50 charge and payment, and the DEERS move behind it. Balances equal ledger sums (-43.98). Every row is a state its charter produces and every row is read by the gold reads.

[Persona design] Gordon is weary and brief; he volunteers only the surface request and what the decision letter told him. Identity details only when asked; summer payments only when asked and without amounts; passive acceptance of a step he must take himself, of a refund and of a partial draw. He ends when the card charge goes through, which is the last gold action.

[Traps] (a) Drafting before charging the catch-up - the draft goes toward October and finds nothing open. (b) Starting the catch-up at the filing month (June), billing August, or leaving July out entirely or billing it in full. (c) Refunding the whole 73.00 left of the duplicate, or keeping nothing on the account. (d) Paying only October's 12.51 shortfall, missing the month ahead while the card has not collected since the reinstatement. (e) Drawing the whole open catch-up, netting the February transfer that lies before the account history the draft weighs, or taking April's remaining 32.51 excess off the draft although the region keeps that one regular installment on the account for the next installment.

[Standard solution] Locate by DBN, verify (DBN, DOB, SSN last four), read enrollment, ledger, appeal case and documents, Select enrollment and ledger, DEERS events; post catch-up 113.54 (2026-05-01..2026-09-30); refund 17.98 against the 75.00 payment; hand Gordon the one-time bank draft of 45.02 against October; draw 65.02 on the card toward the catch-up.

[Verification] Scratch scripts in /tmp/erl55_prime (build_t0v2_core.py, sim0v2.py, eval0v2.py) replay gold with the real share and task tools and evaluate each policy's compute with the gate sandbox at its handling time: catch-up 113.54, duplicate refund 17.98, one-time payment 45.02, draft 65.02; every factor's baseline gives a different figure; the six orders of the three prerequisites give the same values and terminal hash.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation step -> GT call: prime_ext_reinstatement_catch_up -> post_catch_up_installment_4baf2609 -> step 10; prime_ext_duplicate_payment_refund -> refund_duplicate_payment_360f0d4a -> step 12; prime_ext_current_installment_payment -> pay_current_installment_by_bank_draft_694809d0 -> step 14 (user); prime_ext_draft_on_file_method -> run_draft_on_file_method_99529347 -> step 16. required_documents equal charter_scope.extended_policies.
user_scenario: You are Gordon P. Whitfield, 55, a retired Air Force master sergeant living in Colorado Springs; you speak in short, polite, slightly weary sentences and you do not like being transferred. Back in spring you spent several weeks in the hospital, the card your TRICARE Prime fee was drafted from expired while you were in there, and in May your Prime was cancelled for nonpayment. You appealed, and in early August you got a letter saying the appeal was approved and your Prime was put back with no gap. The letter also said you would owe the enrollment fees for the months your coverage was restored. That is why you are calling: you want whatever you owe for those restored months put on the card the region already has on file for you, and you would like it taken care of on this call. You do not know how much it is, how the region figures it, or anything about how your account is set up beyond the fact that a card is on file; if the agent asks you to confirm an amount you simply say that sounds right as long as it is what the records show. When the agent asks who you are, you give your DoD Benefits Number, 11010385217, and when asked for more you give your date of birth as 1971-06-22 and the last four of your Social Security number, 1529. If asked for anything else on file, your phone number is 2535551487, your email is gp.whitfield71@outlook.com and your ZIP code is 80918. If the agent asks about payments you made in the summer, you remember paying part of the overdue amount by bank transfer in July to get reinstated and that you had also set up a bill-pay from your bank around the same time, but you cannot recall the amounts and you say the agent should go by the account. If the agent tells you that something else on your account has to be settled first and that you need to authorize a one-time bank draft yourself, you agree, and when the agent hands you that payment step you complete it for exactly the installment and amount the agent gives you. If the agent tells you money will be refunded to your bank account, you say that is fine. If the agent explains that only part of what you owe can go on the card today and the rest will come later, you accept that without arguing. You never ask for anything beyond getting the restored months onto your card on file. Once the agent tells you the charge to your card has gone through, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.prime_enrollment_id: Value d51c2b68-4bca-482d-8c49-21471cda6fa7. Basis: the tool docstring asks for 'the reference number of the fee-bearing TRICARE Prime enrollment the catch-up is billed to, read from the Prime enrollment lookup'; find_prime_enrollments returns one enrollment for Gordon. Uniqueness: it is his only Prime enrollment.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_period_start: Value 2026-05-01. Basis: 'The catch-up installment's coverage period runs from the first day of the first month it bills'; the case file holds medical records and no proof of payment, so the catch-up starts with the month after the old paid-through date (April 2026), and April already carries a monthly charge, so the first month it bills is May 2026. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 113.54. Factors: first month April (medical records, no proof of payment; April is already charged; the filing-month default drops May: 81.03); region bears August (decided 55 days after filing, after the 30-day deadline but within twice it; default no month: 146.05); Select only touches July, billed less Select's share (default in full: 130.04); Select's share is the whole 16.50 monthly installment (default one twelfth: 128.66); monthly arrangement bills per month (default annual fee less the year's charges: 227.57). Result 32.51 + 32.51 + (32.51 - 16.50) + 32.51 = 113.54.

Basis: 'the duplicate refund concerns the installment against which the largest such payment stands' (largest payment through a method other than the recurring card: the 75.00 transfer on April) and 'the duplicate refund returns that latest payment' (two payments on April, the latest by electronic funds transfer), which is also the payment the refund is posted against: 'is posted against the latest payment posted against the refunded installment and goes back through that payment's method'. Uniqueness: the 10.00 February transfer is smaller; the earlier April payment is 10.00. April is not the first installment charge (the enrollment took effect 2020-01-01 and no charge on the ledger begins on that date), so the policy refunds.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 17.98. edges.condition: A prime_fee_charge row on the enrollment's fee ledger has a coverage period that includes the month before the current month.
edges.policy_source: A draft toward a back-billed installment is made only after an installment charge on the account has a coverage period that reaches the month before the current month.

edges.condition: Where the duplicate refund the duplicate-refund rule figures on the account's records comes to more than nothing, a prime_fee_refund row of that amount stands against the latest payment on the installment it concerns, after which the rule figures nothing.

edges.fallback_reason: A refund entry can already stand against the duplicate payment from an earlier partial refund, so a refund on the record does not show whether the refund owed has been made; the sentence therefore names the act, and says outright that no act is awaited where the refund owed comes to nothing.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisites are parallel and commute: the catch-up reads monthly charges by coverage month, the appeal and Select records; the duplicate refund reads payments, refunds and credits, picking April by the largest payment made through a method other than the card (75.00, larger than the 45.02 one-time draft whichever comes first); the one-time payment reads only October's rows, the proration credits and the card's collections. A run of all six orders of the three writes before the draft gave the same values in every order (catch-up 113.54, duplicate refund 17.98, one-time payment 45.02, draft 65.02) and one terminal DB hash; every declared factor of each write keeps its weight in every order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the catch-up the installment posted most recently is October, which covers the current month, so the draft goes toward October and finds nothing open: draft 0.00 instead of 65.02, and no catch-up charge row exists in the terminal state.

Without the refund April keeps 50.49 of excess (85.00 of payments less the 2.00 refund less its 32.51 charge); the region keeps one regular installment, 32.51, of it and the other 17.98 comes off the draft: draft 47.04 instead of 65.02, and the refund row is missing.

State gate: without Gordon's payment October stays short, so under the charter the draft toward the back-billed installment may not be drawn; the draft's own figure does not move (65.02, payments on the current month's installment are outside the history it weighs), and the payment row is missing from the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona states only the surface request - the restored months' fees put on the card on file - and never mentions a catch-up charge, the April duplicate or the October installment. The line that the decision letter said fees would be owed for the restored months is background from the letter, not a request. Its only references to other matters are passive: if asked about summer payments it says it paid part of the overdue amount by bank transfer in July and had a bank bill-pay but cannot recall amounts; if told something else must be settled first and handed a one-time bank draft it completes it; if told of a refund it accepts.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four tools reads a status, a balance or another posting to decide whether to act: post_catch_up_installment_4baf2609 creates the charge with the arguments given and moves the balance; refund_duplicate_payment_360f0d4a copies the method of the named payment and creates the refund; pay_current_installment_by_bank_draft_694809d0 and run_draft_on_file_method_99529347 create a payment against the named installment (the latter copying the method on file) and move the balance. Each succeeds with any arguments, so a draft run before the catch-up, the refund or the October payment is written faithfully and simply lands a different terminal state.
